transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Meera Rao (VerdantAI CTO), Jon Park (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (FinOps)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage mapping, cost attribution per route, and options for controlling latency vs cost. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted with private VPC for sensitive data. They want concrete examples of route-based chargebacks and a short performance benchmark.

Topics:
- Route definition and tagging model
- Per-route dashboards and filters
- Cost breakdown: per-token, embeddings, and infrastructure overhead
- Batching and KV-cache impact on economics
- Security/compliance: SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope and benchmarking plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Laura, AE on the account, and with me is Samir, our SE. How are you all doing?
[00:08] Meera Rao: Good, thanks. We had a quick sync earlier with Jon, queued up priorities. Really interested to see how you map usage to cost, especially per endpoint, per-route level.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Great, we'll jump into the Console, show the Usage Lens, per-route dashboards, and then go into more detail on how we attribute tokens and GPU time back to routes.
[00:28] Jon Park: One ask up-front: our routes map to microservices, and some calls use long contexts — how does caching and batching change the per-call cost?
[00:36] Samir Patel: Good question. We'll demo a couple of scenarios. Short answer: prefix/KV cache can cut per-token GPU work dramatically for repeated context, and batching helps throughput lower unit cost but with latency tradeoffs.
[00:48] Priya Singh: From finance, we need to see a clean per-route chargeback example. We want to show product teams what they'll be billed and what to optimize.
[00:56] Laura Chen: Perfect. I'll share my screen for the console tour. Apologies if the network blips — sometimes the con-soul (transcription note: "Console") shares are choppy.
[01:08] [screen share starts]
[01:12] Samir Patel: Landing page is the Usage Overview. You can pick time ranges, group by model, route, and user token. I'll select last 30 days and group by route now.
[01:25] Samir Patel: See these tiles — total tokens, billed tokens, average latency, and route count. Notice Route A ("chat-assist") has high billed tokens because of repeated long context, while Route C ("short-search") shows lots of calls but low average tokens.
[01:40] Meera Rao: Are billed tokens equal to tokens sent to model, or do you include tokenization differences?
[01:47] Samir Patel: It matches the runtime billing: tokenization by our tokenizer, plus model-specific token accounting. Small discrepancies can happen if you have custom tokenizers upstream, but we support a tokenizer checksum to align counts.
[01:59] Jon Park: Shows like Route A also have high KV-cache misses, which is the big cost driver?
[02:05] Samir Patel: Exactly. When the KV-hit rate is low, we recompute decoder steps and that drives GPU cycles. You can see KV-cache hit percentage as a filter here.
[02:14] [00:00:15 rough pause, typing sounds]
[02:22] Samir Patel: Now the per-route drill: clicking into Route A, we see traffic split by model variant — redwood-8B-quant and a fallback to redwood-14B in peak hours — plus latency percentiles and cost per 1k calls.
[02:36] Priya Singh: How do you calculate cost per 1k calls? Is that tokens * model rate + infra?
[02:43] Laura Chen: The console shows a composite: token usage * model price + amortized infra overhead (GPU time, bandwidth), plus optional premium for reserved capacity. We also show a breakdown so you can turn off infra to see pure model unit cost.
[02:59] Meera Rao: If we go Dedicated, do we still get per-route cost reporting? We want to keep internal chargebacks without leaking infra rates to product teams.
[03:08] Samir Patel: Yes. Dedicated still reports per-route usage and can produce private chargeback exports. You can export a sanitized CSV where infra columns are obfuscated and only per-route unit rates are shown.
[03:20] Jon Park: Can we tag requests with service_id and environment so we get route+env split?
[03:25] Samir Patel: Absolutely. The SDK supports custom metadata tags; the Console lets you group and filter by any tag key.
[03:32] [01:00:00 slight cross-talk]
[03:36] Samir Patel: Now demoing an anomaly: there was a sudden cost spike yesterday at 11:40. Console flagged an unusual token-per-call increase and traced it to Route B which had a new prompt change. You can click the prompt snapshots to see the exact prompt set.
[03:51] Meera Rao: Prompt snapshots — are these stored raw? We have PII concerns.
[03:56] Laura Chen: By default we store prompt hashes and metadata. Storing raw prompts is opt-in and can be routed to customer-managed retention in Private deployments. We also integrate with KMS so at-rest fields are encrypted.
[04:10] Priya Singh: We need SOC 2 and ISO docs. Also SAML for SSO.
[04:15] Laura Chen: We'll send the security pack. Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private you can enable customer KMS/HSM.
[04:24] Jon Park: Back to batching: can the console simulate what happens if we increase batch window from 20 ms to 80 ms?
[04:31] Samir Patel: Yeah we have a Cost Simulator. I'll pull it up. You can toggle batch windows and cache hit rates to see projected token throughput and cost delta. Watch the projection — increasing batch window reduces cost per token but increases p95 latency.
[04:44] [02:00:00 brief typing pause]
[04:48] Samir Patel: Example: with our sample traffic, increasing batching from 20ms to 80ms saved ~18% on model compute costs but P95 latency went from 120ms to 210ms. We show recommended levers: enable prefix cache, reduce context length, or create a low-latency route pinned to smaller model.
[05:06] Meera Rao: Pinning routes to smaller models — how hard is that operationally?
[05:11] Samir Patel: You can create routing policies: by route, by customer tier, or by latency window. The Console interface has a rollout view — canary, 50/50 split, and automatic fallback if latency SLO missed.
[05:23] Priya Singh: For finance, can we get daily exports of per-route spend to feed into our internal billing?
[05:29] Laura Chen: Yes — scheduled exports via S3 or internal webhooks. Exports include mapping from route => SKU => cost. We can obfuscate infra details for internal teams.
[05:38] Jon Park: For the pilot bench Samir mentioned, can you run the test in our VPC? We prefer private network egress.
[05:45] Samir Patel: We can run a bench from our Dedicated staging or deploy a private inference runner in your VPC for the pilot. We'll need a quick infra checklist from Jon.
[05:54] Meera Rao: Timeline-wise, we need a pilot in two weeks to present to execs. Is that feasible?
[05:59] Laura Chen: Feasible. Proposed: 1) pricing + docs this week, 2) perf bench next week, 3) pilot kickoff week-after.
[06:08] [wrap-up]
[06:12] Laura Chen: Quick recap: Laura shares pricing and security docs, Samir runs bench with Verdant sample set, Jon shares route definitions, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff. Anything else?
[06:22] Priya Singh: Please include example chargeback spreadsheet so we can review with finance.
[06:26] Laura Chen: Will do. Thanks all, we'll follow up on email with calendar invites.
[06:30] Meera Rao: Thanks everyone.
[06:33] [call ends]
